lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 72, which adds a batch skill that runs several issues as grouped PRs.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request seventy-two, which adds a batch skill that runs several issues as grouped pull requests.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
One new skill: an orchestrator that plans, tracks and starts child sessions, and checks on them without reading PR noise.
First it reads each issue and plans the groups: their order, the files they touch, and how many PRs that makes.
You confirm the plan with one reply, and can add a stop point.
It opens a tracking issue with one checklist row per group.
Then it starts a fresh child session for the first group, with a fixed brief.
The child builds, reviews and merges its PR under the repo's rules, and reports back in one line.
Every 90 minutes, a check-in reads only the child's status and whether its PR merged. Then the next group starts.
lines.say: Every ninety minutes, a check-in reads only the child's status and whether its pull request merged. Then the next group starts.

lines.caption: When all groups are merged, or at your stop point, it cancels the check-in, closes the issue and reports.
Why: one session that ran ten issues reached 654 thousand tokens for two PRs, mostly PR noise.
lines.say: Why: one session that ran ten issues reached six hundred fifty-four thousand tokens for two pull requests, mostly P R noise.

lines.caption: The orchestrator never reads CI's comments. It keeps one status per child, like the screenshot audit keeps only its verdict.
The child's brief is copied from the one that ran the last batch's CI change.
A blocked child's question reaches you once, and you answer it in that child's session.
Groups run one at a time, unless the plan you confirmed says their files don't overlap.
Answers go straight to the child, because a relayed approval may be refused there.
And the orchestrator never commits, reviews or merges anything itself.
The PR adds the skill file and this explainer.
To undo it, delete the skill folder. The rules file is unchanged.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was modelled on the repo's skills and the last batch, reviewed by a fresh agent, and not yet run for real.
It follows the upstream merge skill, the screenshot audit's hand-off, and the last batch's brief.
The skill was checked against the issue's steps and risks, and against the tools' real names and fields.
A real batch starts sessions and PRs, so that test is left for you.
The PR changes no code, so CI takes no screenshots.
A fresh agent found nine problems. Eight are fixed, and one was kept on purpose.
The biggest: check-ins could pile up, so now only one is ever pending.
And the child's brief now says to merge only when the merge rule allows it.
CI's first review found nine more. All were fixed in one push.
The tracking issue now holds each group's start time, last PR update and notes, and closed or failed children each have a case.
A full batch, and a blocked child's question, can only be seen once you run it.
Part 3. What comes later.
No issue depends on this one. The next step is a small first batch.
Run it on two doc-only issues, and check the tracking issue ends complete and the orchestrator stays small.
That's the PR: one small session that runs many issues, each in a fresh session of its own.
